profile.name: Yinlin
profile.introduction: Yinlin is a skilled Patroller and powerful Natural Resonator. After being suspended from her duties at the Public Security Bureau, she must now pursue hidden evils in secrecy.
profile.review:
Yinlin is a 5-star Electro Rectifier Hybrid character capable of Coordinated Attacks, Electro and Liberation DMG buffing, decently fast rotations, and relatively good personal damage, who also is quite good in Quickswap teams. Yet, she is characterized by her crucial lack of notoriety in the meta. What does she actually do, and why is she so notoriously replaceable? Let’s explore that more in-depth.

Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts

The focal point of Yinlin’s kit is her Forte Circuit. Her Forte gauge stacks up to 100 points, and it’s regenerated through her Basic Attacks and Skill. Once it’s full, she can cast a Forte Heavy Attack which enables her to trigger Coordinated Attacks. How she does this is through marking enemies. She does so through 3 different stages.

The first of these is Sinner’s Mark. It’s applied on enemies hit by her Intro, Ultimate and Basic Attacks. It can then be upgraded through her Skill, which allows Yinlin to trigger up to 4 Electromagnetic Blasts on enemies hit by her on-field Basic Attacks. Finally, it can be converted into Punishment Mark by her Forte Heavy Attack. As we explained earlier, this enables her to trigger a Coordinated Attack on enemies hit once per second, for a duration of 18s.

One thing worth noting about her Electromagnetic Blasts is that they will individually count towards her Forte and Concerto generation in AoE situations, per enemy hit by them. In other words, in AoE scenarios, Yinlin can charge up her Forte and Concerto gauges much quicker than normal, which can allow her to speed up her rotations drastically. 

The key idea when it comes to Yinlin’s rotation is to apply her Sinner’s Mark and upgrade it through her Skill very quickly, to start generating some Forte and Concerto through a mix of her Skills and Basic or Heavy Attacks. Yinlin has 2 Skills that can be chained consecutively and each generate a great amount of Forte and Concerto, her Ultimate is a nice burst of damage and Concerto as well, and finally her Forte Heavy can finish the rotation as the last big burst of Concerto that she gets.

When it comes to buffs, Yinlin is very simple: the only buff that she can provide is a 20% Electro and 25% Liberation DMG Amplification for 14s, expiring on swap, through her Outro. Her passives do give her a free 15% CRIT Rate and up to 20% ATK for her on-field rotation, but that doesn’t really change much beyond slightly raising her personal damage potential.

Meta Position & Conclusion

As we’re sure you could guess from the above explanation, Yinlin’s only buff being her Outro Skill really doesn’t make her anything special in the Wuthering Waves meta. Every limited Hybrid buffer that followed her had some sort of special buff to give on top of this, like Zhezhi’s Energy generation or Roccia’s team-wide flat ATK buff. Yinlin only has 2 things to contribute to the team, her Outro and personal damage. That’s it.

While Yinlin has a great uptime on her Coordinated Attacks and they deal a lot of personal damage, her rotation is fast, and she gained access to the Empyrean Anthem Echo set which raised her ceiling a bit since her release, she really has nothing too useful to provide to the team due to a crucial lack of unique buffing capabilities. Zhezhi immediately powercrept her in the Jinhsi team very shortly after Jinhsi’s own release, and Xiangli Yao and Calcharo were never good to begin with. In other words: Ever since her release, Yinlin did nothing special, and was nothing special.

While she has Quickswap potential, and she has personal damage, Changli is simply an upgraded Yinlin in this role, and Lynae has completely powercrept Yinlin in any team she could ever exist in, Quickswap or not. She has way, way more buffs, a modern and cohesive kit, and her similar personal damage and rotation time make Lynae so much more useful than Yinlin in all Liberation DMG teams, including Electro ones, it’s not even comparable. As a final nail in the coffin, practically no Electro damage dealers have been released since Xiangli Yao, and when they did, F2P options wound up better than Yinlin. Take Augusta with Mortefi, or Hsin with Electro Rover, or Suoming with Sanhua as examples. Electro/Liberation is a combination of damage types Yinlin needs to be present on a character for her to be justified on any team, and no damage dealer has released with those damage types since Xiangli Yao, where Lynae powercrept Yinlin, and where Changli has always been better in Quickswap.

In conclusion, Yinlin is one of the worst limited characters in Wuthering Waves. From a meta standpoint, we advise skipping this character. Unless you really, really are fond of Yinlin, generally speaking, the investment is not worth it. She retains some okay-ish usability in a select few teams if you already own her though, so she isn’t completely unusable if she is present on your account. Still, her weapon Stringmaster is a great generalist Rectifier DPS choice and is much, much higher priority than Yinlin herself considering her current meta situation (even still, we currently recommend pulling Signature Rectifiers for the DPS you choose to pull rather than Stringmaster).
profile.pros:
• Highly Quickswap-friendly;

  • Stringmaster is a great weapon.
profile.cons:
• Stringmaster is a better pull than the character itself.

  • No, seriously, we mean this, she’s completely outshined by Lynae in every team she could exist in, or other Quickswap characters like Changli, or other Coordinated Attackers like Hsin or Zhezhi, modern Electro teams don’t want her, even Jianxin isn’t too terrible of a replacement for her in Liberation damage teams.

  • Highly prone to interruption in non-Quickswap rotations.

profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to Play

Yinlin’s rotation goal is to get her Forte Heavy Attack and cast it as quickly as possible by restoring her Forte gauge as quickly as possible.

Echo Timing

Transform into Nightmare: Tempest Mephis (Empyrean Anthem) or Impermanence Heron (Moonlit Clouds) after casting her Forte Heavy Attack (outside of Quickswap). If possible, in Quickswap, it’s strongly recommended to cast them before Yinlin’s Intro in order to Swap Cancel Chameleon Cipher to finish her rotation.

Standard Rotation

This rotation is the best way to quickly generate Forte while having a nice way to Swap Cancel your Echo cast. Recommended for most use cases outside of Quickswap.

  • Intro

  • Basic 4

  • Skill: Magnetic Roar

  • Heavy Attack (Interrupt via Skill at 1 of 2 hits)

  • Skill: Lightning Execution (Cancel animation when Yinlin hits the ground via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Basic 1

  • Heavy: Chameleon Cipher

  • Echo (Swap)

  • Outro

Tip: In AoE situations, Yinlin can Swap Cancel her Forte Heavy into Outro thanks to extra Concerto/Forte generation from doing more Electromagnetic Blasts. If you cast her Echo Skill before her rotation starts, this can represent a noticeable time save!

Optimized Opener

The Opener rotation below is one of the ways Yinlin can optimize her rotation in Quickswap. This is only practical in single-target since you don’t need this in AoE thanks to multiple Electromagnetic Blasts. With that being said, the focus of  this rotation is to fully Swap Cancel her Forte Heavy so that all of its Concerto generation happens after Outro and transposes into the next rotation, enabling for faster Loops afterwards (since Yinlin gets the extra Concerto required to Swap Cancel her Forte Heavy on every rotation that follows).  You can do this like so:

  • Switch-in from any other character in combat

  • Basic 2

  • Heavy Attack (Interrupt via Skill at 1 of 2 hits)

  • Skill: Magnetic Roar

  • Skill: Lightning Execution (Swap)

  • Switch-in from any other character in combat

  • Basic 2

  • Heavy Attack (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate after both hits)

  • Ultimate

  • Heavy Attack (Swap)

  • Intro

  • Heavy: Chameleon Cipher (Swap)

  • Outro

Then you can either do fully Quickswap loops from here, or go back into the Standard Rotation and go faster on every Loop (just make sure to cast Yinlin’s Echo before her Intro in the latter case).

Additional Tips & Tricks

While we already mentioned most Quickswap tips in the above sections, Yinlin has good Swap Cancel windows in the form of her Basic 4 after Intro, her Lightning Execution Skill, and her Heavy Attacks. These can provide a good amount of Forte quickly while off-field. However, keep in mind her Magnetic Roar Skill cannot be Swap Cancelled, since you really want to combo it into Lightning Execution which requires Yinlin to stay on-field (it generates a lot more Concerto and Forte than any of her Basic Attacks, so you’d be slowing your rotation down to a halt by skipping out on it).

You can use the above Swap Cancel windows to significantly speed up Yinlin’s rotation by executing parts of it during other characters’ rotations!

skills.name: Zapstring's Dance
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Yinlin controls the puppet "Zapstring" to perform up to 4 attacks, dealing Electro DMG.

Heavy Attack

Consumes Stamina to control puppet "Zapstring" to attack, dealing Electro DMG.

Mid-air Attack

Consumes Stamina to control the puppet "Zapstring" to perform a Plunging Attack, dealing Electro DMG.

Dodge Counter

Use Basic Attack after a successful Dodge to attack the target, dealing Electro DMG.

skills.name: Magnetic Roar
skills.description:
Magnetic Roar

The puppet "Zapstring" deals Electro DMG to the target, and puts Yinlin into the Execution Mode.

Execution Mode

Basic Attack and Dodge Counter will trigger 1 Electromagnetic Blast when hitting a target. Each stage of Basic Attack or Dodge Counter can only trigger 1 Electromagnetic Blast, up to 4 times.

Electromagnetic Blast

Attack all targets marked with Resonance Circuit Sinner's Mark, dealing Electro DMG.

Lightning Execution

Use Resonance Skill after casting Resonance Skill Magnetic Roar to cast Lightning Execution to attack the target, dealing Electro DMG. If Resonance Skill Lightning Execution is not activated in a while or this Character is switched, this Skill will be put on Cooldown.

skills.name: Thundering Wrath
skills.description: Command "Zapstring" to call for thunder to fall upon a large range, dealing Electro DMG.

skills.name: Chameleon Cipher
skills.description:
Chameleon Cipher

When Yinlin's "Judgment Points" is full, her Heavy Attack is replaced with Chameleon Cipher, which consumes all "Judgment Points" to attack the target, dealing Electro DMG. When it hits a target marked with Sinner's Mark, the Sinner's Mark is replaced with Punishment Mark, lasting for 18 seconds.

Sinner's Mark

Normal Attack Zapstring's Dance, Resonance Liberation Thundering Wrath, and Intro Skill Roaring Strorm will apply Sinner's Mark on hit. Sinner's Mark is removed when Yinlin exits.

"Punishment Mark"

When a target marked with Punishment Mark is damaged, Judgement Strike will fall, dealing Electro DMG to all targets marked with Punishment Mark. This can be triggered up to once per second.

Judgment Points

  • Yinlin can hold up to 100 Judgement Points.

  • When Normal Attack Zapstring's Dance hits a target, restores "Judgment Points".

  • Upon casting Resonance Skill Magnetic Roar, restores "Judgment Points".

  • When Resonance Skill Electromagnetic Blast hits a target, restores "Judgment Points".

skills.name: Deadly Focus

skills.name: Raging Storm
skills.description: Command puppet "Zapstring" to attack, dealing Electro DMG in a large range.

skills.name: Strategist
skills.description: The next character (or other characters on a nearby team that activates an Outro Skill) gains 20% Electro DMG Deepen, and 25% Resonance Liberation DMG Deepen for 14 seconds or until the Character is switched.

dupes.dupe1: Resonance Skill Magnetic Roar and Lightning Execution deal 70% more damage.
dupes.dupe2: Resonance Skill Electromagnetic Blast recovers an additional 5 "Judgement Point(s)" and 5 Resonance Energy on hit.
dupes.dupe3: Forte Circuit Judgment Strike's DMG multiplier is increased by 55%.
dupes.dupe4: When Forte Circuit Judgment Strike hits a target, the ATK of all team members is increased by 20% for 12s.
dupes.dupe5: Resonance Liberation Thundering Wrath deals 100% extra damage to targets with Forte Circuit's Sinner's Mark or Punishment Mark.
dupes.dupe6: In the first 30s after casting Resonance Liberation Thundering Wrath, when Yinlin's Basic Attack hits a target, Furious Thunder will be triggered, dealing Electro DMG equal to 419.59% of Yinlin's ATK. Every Basic Attack hit can trigger Furious Thunder 1 time, up to 4 times. This is considered Resonance Skill DMG.

weapons.Comment: Yinlin's signature Rectifier is easily one of the best generalist options in the game and her best in slot. It gives massive ATK, CRIT Rate and DMG Bonus buffs, with an ATK% buff that's only further increased in quickswap which makes it stand even higher above the options below.

Cantarella's Signature weapon provides super high CRIT DMG and solid ATK and Basic DMG Bonus stats. While Yinlin does tend to overcap on CRIT Rate when running her Signature weapon, it isn't an issue on this weapon which makes it one of the best alternatives Yinlin has available.
Slightly worse version of Whispers of Sirens, giving the same base stats and benefits but less Basic DMG Bonus.

This weapon has a lower CRIT Rate secondary stat but gets higher Base ATK as a trade-off. On top of its 8% DEF Ignore effect, it also provides Yinlin enough CRIT Rate to CRIT consistently without overcapping, making it a great choice for her.
Best permanently available option for Yinlin, lacks CRIT stat boosts but gives a lot of ATK and Energy Regen in exchange.
ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Yinlin, who does not benefit from this weapon's Spectro Frazzle-oriented effects. Also runs into CRIT Rate overcap issues.

Best 4-star weapon option, this Battle Pass Exclusive gets an easy-to-activate ATK buff when casting Ultimate and also gives a nice CRIT secondary stat but has lower Base ATK as a 4-star making it worse than any 5-star option.
Second Battle Pass Exclusive choice which gives an easy to activate ATK and Basic DMG Bonus buff but gives lower ATK than Augment which makes it a worse option overall if Augment is available.
Easy-to-activate ATK buffs make this weapon the best F2P 4-star choice for Yinlin, but it does not provide any CRIT stats and has a low Base ATK which makes it easily replaced by the above options.

echoes.Comment: Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

echoes.Comment: Offers an unconditional 10% Energy Regen% and 80% Coordinated DMG boost. Also grants a passive supportive effect upon a Coordinated Attack CRIT, giving 20% ATK to the on-field active character. Offers a nice blend of personal damage and buffing.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Offers 12% Electro DMG and 12% Resonance Skill DMG boost when placed in the Main Echo slot, awkward to use due to the long Transform animation.

echoes.Comment: This set sacrifices Yinlin's personal damage in order to provide higher buffing to a single character. It provides an extra 10% Energy Regen to the wielder unconditionally and gives 22.5% ATK to the incoming character for 15s after casting Outro skill.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: The best and only real option 5P Moonlit Clouds has, as it grants an extra 12% DMG Bonus on top of the ATK boost to the next character that Moonlit Clouds would usually give. Additionally restores a lot of Energy to the caster when it deals damage.

echoStats.Name: yinlin
echoStats.Substats: Energy Regen (Until Satisfied) > CRIT Rate = CRIT DMG > ATK% > ATK = Resonance Skill DMG%

skillPriority.Order: Forte Circuit, Res. Liberation, Res. Skill, Basic Attack, Intro Skill

synergies.Comment: Yinlin's best synergy nowadays is with Main DPS Iuno, as Iuno has one of the highest Liberation DMG potentials in the game and Yinlin is only outclassed by a Ciaccona with her Signature weapon equipped. Yinlin provides good on and off-field damage as well as 25% Liberation DMG Amplify to Iuno which makes her a close second best choice to Ciaccona.

Yinlin's Coordinated Attacks, personal damage, small buffs she provides to Jinhsi's Ultimate via Outro and general buffs with Echoes, and her swap cancel windows at a less casual level, make Jinhsi and Yinlin a competitive pair to Zhezhi (while being a bit worse), and one of the best teams in the game.

Due to Yinlin's good personal off-field damage, but most importantly her extremely important 20% Electro and 25% Liberation DMG Amplify on Outro, she can buff Xiangli Yao by ludicrous amounts and make him a top DPS.

Yinlin should only be considered in Augusta teams as a worse option than Mortefi. This is because while she has slightly higher personal damage, it doesn't compensate for her smaller amount of Outro and extra ATK% buffs (which Mortefi easily accesses via the Static Mist pistol and his S6). Additionally, her higher rotation time ultimately makes her only worth slotting on Augusta's team if your Mortefi is already taken by another character or if you like Yinlin (as technically it's Yinlin's new best team, just not the other way around).

Similarly to Xiangli Yao, Yinlin's good personal off-field damage and her extremely important 20% Electro and 25% Liberation DMG Amplify on Outro buffs Calcharo a major amount, while also being able to trade those buffs off for consistency by abusing each other's many Swap Cancel windows, making the pair natural.

Yinlin is actually the character Youhu buffs the most, due to Yinlin having the highest personal damage of any Coordinated Attack DPS in the game and her ability to amplify Coordinated Attack DMG by 100% on Outro. As a result, the pairing is natural, while it doesn't compare to 5 star supports.

One of the usual Healing Support options that can slot into any team. Super easy to use, provides amazing team-wide ATK% buffs and 15% DMG Amplify with one of the fastest rotations in the game. Enjoy.

Similar to Verina, a premium Healing Support option who can not only slot into any team, but also provide insane 12.5% Crit Rate, 25% Crit DMG, 25% ATK and 15% DMG Amplify buffs to your whole team. One of the best but also easy to use characters in the game.
